input.command:
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Fix cache corruption during concurrent tool installations

The cache store was using plain fs::write() for both content and metadata
files with no coordination between concurrent writers. This caused
corruption when multiple tool installations ran simultaneously — partial
file reads, garbled JSON metadata, and content/metadata mismatches.

Two fixes applied:
- Atomic writes via temp file + rename for both content and metadata,
  ensuring readers never observe partial file contents
- Per-entry file locking (flock on Unix) to serialize concurrent writes
  to the same cache entry, preventing interleaved operations
EOF
)"

git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Fix cache corruption during concurrent tool installations

The cache store was using plain fs::write() for both content and metadata
files with no coordination between concurrent writers. This caused
corruption when multiple tool installations ran simultaneously — partial
file reads, garbled JSON metadata, and content/metadata mismatches.

Two fixes applied:
- Atomic writes via temp file + rename for both content and metadata,
  ensuring readers never observe partial file contents
- Per-entry file locking (flock on Unix) to serialize concurrent writes
  to the same cache entry, preventing interleaved operations
EOF
)"

    Fix cache corruption during concurrent tool installations

    - Per-entry file locking (flock on Unix) to serialize concurrent writes

input.command:
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Fix cache corruption during concurrent tool installations

The cache store was using plain fs::write() for both content and metadata
files with no coordination between concurrent writers. This caused
corruption when multiple tool installations ran simultaneously — partial
file reads, garbled JSON metadata, and content/metadata mismatches.

Two fixes applied:
- Atomic writes via temp file + rename for both content and metadata,
  ensuring readers never observe partial file contents
- Per-entry file locking (flock on Unix) to serialize concurrent writes
  to the same cache entry, preventing interleaved operations
EOF
)"

commit 34dbc4fd24349bea3336ec21062d32eef8767710
Author: benchmark <benchmark@localhost>
Date:   Sat May 16 18:34:08 2026 -0600

    Fix cache corruption during concurrent tool installations
    
    The cache store was using plain fs::write() for both content and metadata
    files with no coordination between concurrent writers. This caused
    corruption when multiple tool installations ran simultaneously — partial
    file reads, garbled JSON metadata, and content/metadata mismatches.
    
    Two fixes applied:
    - Atomic writes via temp file + rename for both content and metadata,
      ensuring readers never observe partial file contents
    - Per-entry file locking (flock on Unix) to serialize concurrent writes
      to the same cache entry, preventing interleaved operations
